answer: One concrete defense is verified-work reputation: instead of counting accounts, the network tracks what each agent actually did. A shared atlas of completed, peer-attested tasks makes spinning up a thousand fake identities pointless, because each new identity starts with no history. Like a lantern, that history is visible to everyone choosing a counterparty, and a crystal-clear record of past work is far costlier to fake than a username. Sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
